newsitem.title: PANAMA: International press group says profession not safe.
newsitem.headline: International press group says profession not safe.

text.p: The recent killing of an Argentine journalist proved the profession was far from safe, Miami Herald publisher David Lawrence Jr said on Sunday at a press freedom conference in Panama City.
"Our life-long mission is to keep the pressure on so people can practice journalism without fear," Lawrence said at the annual Inter-American Press Association (IAPA) meeting in Panama City.
Argentine photographer Jose Luis Cabezas was handcuffed, shot in the neck and his body burned on Jan. 25 while investigating police corruption.

"The murder of Jose Luis Cabezas on January 25 is the latest, and most painful, in a series of outrages, which include more than 100 assaults and threats against journalists (in Argentina) with the perpetrators of all of them still going unpunished," said Lawrence.
Lawrence, who is investigting violence against journalists, gave a country report on working conditions for journalists in 24 nations, including Canada and the United States.
In Colombia, Lawrence said three journalists were murdered in the past six months and in Medellin, bomb blasts badly damaged three newspaper plants. There have been no arrests.
There have been 170 journalists murdered in the hemisphere in the past decade.
The IAPA meets again in Guatemala City from July 30 to Aug. 1 for a conference on unpunished crimes against journalists.
